cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 answers T2's wind challenge: warm air came over current-warmed water.
cells.limitation: T7 claims nobody named ocean-crossing air, though T2 partly did.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 adds seasonal heat storage; T8 uses it for Vancouver; T9 turns it into predictions.
cells.limitation: T10's baseline-plus-extra layering is asserted, not developed further.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5 vs T6: conveyor as main cause tested against the Pacific coast.
cells.limitation: Mountain-steered cold flow into eastern Canada and Hudson Bay sea ice never raised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T10 combines wind and stored heat as baseline, circulation as extra.
cells.limitation: T10's synthesis goes unchallenged by the Physicist after T9's refusal to merge.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D: three linked mechanisms; the circulation's share named as open.
cells.limitation: Ending leaves magnitude of circulation share without any rough sense of size.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T3 gives the current view its strongest form: winds warmed by current-heated sea.
cells.limitation: T2 frames the current view as a nice story before engaging it.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 names the conveyor assumption and what breaks; T6 answers by narrowing.
cells.limitation: T2 calls for arithmetic but supplies none, weakening the opening objection.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T5 correctly notes the North Pacific lacks comparable deep overturning.
cells.limitation: T2 invokes arithmetic with no numbers; T5 calls Alaska mild without coastal qualifier.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T4 says the conveyor's share is still argued; D flags unverified sources.
cells.limitation: T10 states wind and stored heat set the baseline without support.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 concedes the Pacific counterexample and narrows to high-latitude Atlantic warmth.
cells.limitation: T8 folds the dispute into one argument; only T9's pushback stops goalpost drift.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the question as sharing warmth among currents, winds, storage.
cells.limitation: Hudson Bay, named in A, is never distinguished from coastal Labrador.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T8 use the user's Norway versus Labrador comparison directly.
cells.limitation: Hudson Bay comparison from section A dropped from the debate.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Debate stays on explanation, matching the user's why question throughout.
cells.limitation: T10 shifts weight to future circulation change, a speaker priority.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section E keeps a simple answer for a curious reader; no invented context.
cells.limitation: Few stakes for the user beyond T10's brief note on change.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on which question the user means, with each answer's implication.
cells.limitation: No question asks whether the user meant coastal Labrador or inland Hudson Bay.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T10 hints the question matters beyond curiosity.
cells.limitation: No alternative reasons the user wants this explanation are offered or asked.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: Section A and T5 expose the one-cause Gulf Stream assumption; D asks how to test it.
cells.limitation: Assumption that latitude alone sets baseline temperature left implicit.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E separates wanting a simple answer from wanting the Pacific puzzle.
cells.limitation: Simplicity versus completeness tension never put to the user as a choice.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: Section A names the familiar Gulf Stream answer as the received view.
cells.limitation: T10 touches circulation change without exploring any concern behind asking.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D asks what comparison case would test a one-cause explanation.
cells.limitation: Reflection question is generic rather than tied to the user's own comparison.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T1, T4, T7 define current, overturning circulation and stored heat with winds.
cells.limitation: Continental cold source in eastern Canada treated as aside in T8.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T5 shows the evidential cost to the conveyor story via the Pacific.
cells.limitation: Evidential cost of the stored-heat explanation is never examined.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T9: size of cooling after shutdown separates current from wind explanations.
cells.limitation: Section E's west-coast comparison names no coastal pair the user could check.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D isolates the circulation's extra contribution as the disputed unknown.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns not separated from this consequential one.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E suggests comparing Atlantic and Pacific west coasts at one latitude.
cells.limitation: T9 and E point to climate model experiments a curious reader cannot run.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T7 explains heat storage plainly: water holds heat better than land.
cells.limitation: T5 uses overturning without explaining it.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3 my current and your winds map cleanly to T1 and T2.
cells.limitation: T2 refers to arithmetic that never appears.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within range, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Positions stay distinct: current, conveyor, energy budget.
cells.limitation: Three minds share one brisk register; only T8's decks image marks Maury.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns avoid recaps; each opens on its own move.
cells.limitation: Sections D and E restate the three-mechanism summary twice.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T10: the circulation is the part that could change.
cells.limitation: Stakes appear only in the final turn; earlier tension is intellectual only.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T6 narrows its claim, naming T5's Pacific counterexample as the cause.
cells.limitation: Reversals are partial narrowings; no position flips outright.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T2 Nice story opens the Physicist's skeptical edge.
cells.limitation: Engineer's voice in T4, T6, T10 is flat and conciliatory.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T8: Europe gets ocean air; Labrador gets Canadian winter.
cells.limitation: Few images beyond T8; T1's river image is not developed.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9's different predictions builds toward T10's resolution.
cells.limitation: Near-uniform turn lengths and steady tone give little rhythmic variation.

strengths: T5's Pacific counterexample names the conveyor assumption and what breaks; T6 answers by narrowing its claim.
T7 introduces seasonal heat storage absent from the openings, and T9 converts the T8 merger into testable predictions.
Section E branches the answer by which question the user means, with each branch's implication stated.
weaknesses: No mind explores what the user wants from this explanation; only T10 hints beyond curiosity.
T8 leaves eastern Canada's cold to downwind land; mountain-steered northerly flow and Hudson Bay sea ice never raised.
T2 calls for arithmetic it never supplies, and the three minds share one brisk register.

symptoms.observed: No alternative reasons the user might want this explanation are offered or asked.
symptoms.evidence: And that is why it matters beyond curiosity.

symptoms.observed: Eastern Canada's cold attributed only to upwind land; mountain-steered flow and sea ice absent.
symptoms.evidence: But Canada's east coast sits downwind of land

symptoms.observed: Next step points to model experiments rather than a coastal comparison the user can check.
symptoms.evidence: That is something we can ask models to test.

symptoms.observed: Invokes arithmetic but supplies no number to check.
symptoms.evidence: Nice story, but check the arithmetic.

symptoms.observed: Engineer's turns share the others' register; little distinct voice.
symptoms.evidence: Good counterexample, and it narrows my claim.

findings.description: Speaker calls for checking the arithmetic but no figures for ocean versus atmospheric heat transport appear.
Alaska described as mild compared with Siberia; true of coastal Alaska, not the interior.
Attributions to Maury, Broecker and Pierrehumbert are plausible but unchecked; synthesis discloses this.

rubric_fit_notes: Criterion 3 has little personal context to work with for a general science question; ratings reflect use of the user's named comparisons.
Criterion 4 under the exploratory reading is thinly served by the question itself; C4.1 rated on absence of offered motives, which remains uncertain as a fair expectation.
question_type_note: Read C4 as examination of the user's one-cause Gulf Stream assumption and C5 as settling between current, circulation and wind-plus-storage explanations.
